boundary: Pass 5968 identifies the unit classes as PGL(2,q) BY DEFINITION -- invertible matrices modulo scalars -- which is a restatement, not a discovery. Its value is that it names what the other lane's '6 units' are. Pass 5970's q=2 uniqueness argument is over the seven q tested

pass_5968_the_units_are_pgl.reading: the unit classes ARE PGL(2,q) -- invertible matrices modulo scalars is the projective linear group by definition, so this is a restatement rather than a coincidence. What it buys is a NAME for the other lane's six units: they are PGL(2,2) = S_3, of order 6, which is why they form K_3,3

pass_5969_coclique_formula.quadric: Q+(3,q) is the hyperbolic quadric, a (q+1)x(q+1) grid with two rulings

pass_5970_why_q2_is_unique.conclusion: q=2 is the ONLY case where the matrix algebra IS the polar space, unquotiented, carrying a symplectic form. That is precisely why the other lane's doily identification is exact rather than approximate, and it is a sharper statement than 'characteristic two matters'
pass_5970_why_q2_is_unique.q4_and_q8: have (b) but not (a) -- characteristic 2, but a genuine quotient is needed
two_conditions: (a) scalars are trivial, since q-1 = 1, so NO quotient is taken and the 15 nonzero matrices ARE the 15 points
(b) characteristic 2, so the determinant polarization is alternating and the ambient space is symplectic

pass_5971_the_full_family.note: the totals are exactly the point counts of W(3,q), which is (q^2+1)(q+1)
